newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn cuts corporation tax rate to 36 pct.
newsitem.headline: Quinn cuts corporation tax rate to 36 pct.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Wednesday that he was cutting the corporation tax rate to 36 percent from 38 percent.
Quinn also told parliament that he would cut the 30 percent rate of corporation tax to 28 percent.
The taxable income tax band to which the 28 percent rate applies will remain at 50,000 pounds, he said.
Quinn said companies with profits of 50,000 pounds or less each year will now be paying tax at 28 percent as compared with 40 percent in 1994. There were some 20,000 such companies, he said.
"This is a real reduction of nearly one third in the tax rate for the small and medium-sized Irish companies concerned," he said.

He said the government was studying the desired corporation tax structure over the longer term, "bearing in mind the central importance of the 10 percent rate for inward investment included in the IFSC.
"I am conscious of the need to clarify this issue at an early date and I would hope...to make an announcement before too long."
Most Dublin-based economists had forecast a two percentage point in corporation tax to match the reduction at last year's budget.
